prose.summary: Mansha cannot confirm whether the cosmetic skin creams qualify for the CEPA rate yet, because information is missing. If the product qualifies, the estimated saving is 12000.00 AED. The missing information is the 6-digit HS code for the emollients in row 2 of the bill of materials.
prose.classification: The cosmetic skin creams are classified under tariff line 33049990, which is described as Other beauty or make-up preparations. Mansha's confidence in this classification is medium, and the exporter should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate—the standard duty charged when no trade-agreement preference is claimed—is 20%, while the CEPA rate—the reduced rate under the trade agreement—is 0%. If the product qualifies, the estimated saving is 12000.00 AED. Note that the CEPA rate applies to Basic Customs Duty only, so other import charges such as IGST are still paid even when the CEPA rate is 0%.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH), meaning each non-originating input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the product, and value addition (VA) of at least 40%, which is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. The origin check cannot be completed yet because the bill of materials is incomplete. Specifically, the emollients in row 2 currently lack a 6-digit HS code, which is needed to check the CTSH requirement. No checks were run, so the origin result remains unconfirmed.

notes.text: The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, regardless of what the product-specific rule says.
The acceptance of electronic certificates and their upload to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports.

The duty saving is estimated on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 40%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
